Its a great central location. The price is affordable and most importantly there is no parking fee. There are a lot of hotels who charge for parking in addition to the room reservation which I don't understand. If you traveling for business or leisure this a great place. The rooms are updated. The beds are comfortable not hard. The TV channels are good. I stayed 3 days and my room was cleaned and I had plenty of towels. I just want to emphasize that I traveled solo so my perspective is coming from that place. I've seen a lot of couples and solo travels at the hotel during my stay but not many families with little children so please keep that in mind. Either way its a great place because of location, price and cleanliness which are extremely important nowadays.

text.text:
Aged, Musty, and Not Worth the Price

We stayed at Four Points by Sheraton Orlando International Drive expecting a comfortable stay based on the Marriott Bonvoy name, but the experience was extremely disappointing.

The room had a stagnant, moldy, almost cat-pee odor that appeared to be coming from the bathroom. With no airflow, sealed windows, and no balcony or lanai, the smell lingered and made the room feel damp and stuffy the entire stay.

The property is clearly aging. The carpet felt worn and old, the furniture looked dated, and the room had that humid, musty feel common in buildings that haven’t been properly updated. The bathroom showed signs of age as well, with lingering mildew odors and poor ventilation.

Soundproofing is minimal. You can hear hallway noise, doors slamming, and outside traffic from International Drive. The air conditioner was loud and cycled frequently, making it hard to sleep.

Other disappointments:

• Outdated interior and worn furnishings
• Damp, stale smell that never cleared
• No fresh air or ventilation options
• Thin walls and noticeable noise
• Bathroom ventilation issues
• Overall “tired” and neglected feel

Parking was $20 per day, which feels excessive given the large surface lot and available space. Hidden costs like this add to the frustration, especially when the room itself is already overpriced for what you get.

Pros:
• Convenient location near Universal Studios
• Easy access to International Drive dining and attractions

Cons:
• Strong unpleasant odor in the room
• Poor ventilation and sealed windows
• Aging property with worn interiors
• Noise and loud AC unit
• Extra daily parking fee
• Poor value for the price

We booked expecting a reliable Sheraton-level stay, but the property felt neglected and outdated. Between the smell, lack of airflow, and extra fees, it was not a comfortable experience — and we would not return.

Reservation made in January for 9 nights beginning in September 2025 (holidays).
On the plus side:
The rooms are spacious, equipped with a small refrigerator, microwave, coffee maker, and numerous USB ports. The bed was quite comfortable.

The sink drain was faulty.
The chandelier in the bathroom was missing. The light bulb and wires were visible.
The two ice machines were broken....

No problems with the staff, the room was cleaned, towels and toilet paper were replaced.

The reception and check-in desk were more than average.

Although the hotel is well located, this experience remains very average. I do not recommend it, given the other options in the surrounding area.

I used Choice Rewards points to book a complimentary night at this hotel, and the experience has been nothing short of shocking. The front desk staff checked me in on their system, but then refused to actually give me a room unless I paid a $150 deposit — even though other guests were being charged $100 or less. When I asked why my deposit was higher, I was given no explanation at all.

To make matters worse, they never cancelled my reservation in the Choice system. They marked me as “checked in” and told Choice I was already in the room, which is completely false. Because of this, Choice customer service believed I was accommodated, and I was left outside in the cold and rain with nowhere to go late at night.

I’ve been a Choice Diamond member for almost 3 years, and I have NEVER been treated like this. I called Choice multiple times for help, and I was hung up on repeatedly because the hotel was reporting that I was already checked into my room. Meanwhile, I was literally outside the property with my luggage, soaking wet and freezing.

The room is not double-booked, not unavailable, and not occupied whatsoever the front desk simply refused to honor my reward stay while still keeping me marked as checked in. This is extremely shady behavior and feels like the property is scamming Choice by claiming guests are in rooms that they never provided.
There was no compassion, no problem-solving, no attempt to help, and no honesty. Just refusal, runaround, and misrepresentation.

I have stayed at Choice properties across the country for years without issues, so I am genuinely stunned by the treatment I received here. I will not return to this location, and I strongly urge other Choice members to be cautious when booking this property.

4 Star Hotel at a 3 Star price! Excellence throughout!

We thought we were only staying here one night when we arrived in Orlando, planning to find an AirBnB, but we liked it so much we extended for a couple weeks.

Joshua at the front desk was an excellent example of the high caliber staff we interacted with throughout our stay. Always warm and friendly, always going out of their way to make us feel welcome. They seem genuinely happy to be hosting you.

The hotel itself is well appointed, modern and immaculately clean in the common areas and the room. It's pet friendly, which we love, and floors were cleaned properly, which is something we find other hotels miss.

Pool, gym and other amenities were great. No free breakfast, but frankly we preferred the option to buy a higher quality, ala carte' breakfast versus the generally bland, low quality options you get at "free breakfast" in other hotels we have stayed.

Great selection of snacks and well presented.

There's grass for the dogs and you are right in the middle of all the theme parks so access everywhere is quick. Great restaurants, Walmart, all the theme parks... and a great mini-golf course with live alligators (LOL) across the street.

Will definitely stay here again the next time we are in Orlando!

text.text:
Date of stay - June 2026

2 Adults and 1 child

Great hotel, clean, rooms made up every single day and towels changed daily also.

Service second to none.

The hotel has a policy of quiet hours after 10pm which was good too know as sound can travel from adjoining rooms and at one point I thought I might of needed to engage with the staff to intervene which they strictly enforce, but thankfully, the overly loud room next door left.

Not sure why the cheap toilet paper as we just ended up using twice as much, small thing really.

The pool is very shallow, never getting any deeper than roughly 3ft, so swimming is difficult, but as relief from the hot humid environment is 1st class. Brace yourself for a hefty bar bill if drinking at the pool or the bar in there hotel, very much in keeping with big city prices.

The cafe is good for some things such as pizza, but for a good breakfast IHop is a five minute walk away which is almost impossible to finish for less money, the breakfast in the hotel is meger at best.

The free shuttle buses to the parks are great, Andy the early access to the parks is worth it's weight in gold.

Getting around - if you're staying local, Ubers are cheap, efficient, friendly and plentiful. If you're planning get out further afield, hire a car for those days, but for us, there was no point as we had free shuttle buses.

Eating out from this location - we found Icon Park a really good option which is a 5 dollar Uber away where there are a good range of restaurants for all tastes.

All in all though, 4.5 stars from me, would definitely stay here again.

I would like to provide feedback regarding my recent stay.

First, I was supposed to be notified when my room was ready, but I never received a call or text. Because I was waiting for that notification, I stayed longer at the park and became extremely exhausted while waiting to check in. I finally called around 6:00 PM and was told my room had been ready, but there were system issues. If the system was having problems, someone could have called me to let me know instead of leaving me waiting without any communication.

Second, I requested a late checkout, but it appears that information was not properly communicated to housekeeping. A housekeeper came to my door shortly after 9:00 AM even though the normal checkout time was 11:00 AM and I had been approved for a late checkout. Later, I called the front desk and requested a luggage cart be sent up when I was preparing to leave. Instead, a housekeeper arrived with a different piece of equipment, and when I explained that I had requested a luggage cart, another employee told me I would have to go downstairs and get it myself, despite the front desk advising that one would be sent to my room.

To make matters worse, another housekeeper knocked on my door around 11:20 AM while I was having a conversation with my daughter. Since I had been approved for a 12:00 PM checkout, it was very frustrating and disruptive to have multiple interruptions. There seemed to be a significant lack of communication between the front desk and housekeeping staff, which negatively impacted my privacy and peace during my stay.

Finally, the café staff gave me a difficult time when I attempted to use my dining voucher for juice. We spent approximately 30 minutes discussing something that should have been simple to resolve, which was both frustrating and unnecessary.

Overall, the recurring communication issues between departments created an unpleasant experience and significantly affected the quality of my stay. I hope these concerns are addressed so future guests do not encounter the same problems. I would not be back to this hotel at all

text.text: Surfside Inn & Suites was great for the price. Our only complaint was how much noise you can hear in the room. If the noise doesn't bother you, I recommend this hotel. I had ear plugs that I could put in to block it out so it wasn't a problem for me, but something to be aware of - sacrifice price for noise. Despite the noise, I would stay here again. I like the Surfside better than the Dockside because it is a little smaller, plus the bus between the hotel and City walk/Universal Orlando/Islands of Adventure stops at Surfside before Dockside.

I recently stayed at Cambria during my Universal trip and overall had a really good experience. The hotel feels very newly renovated, modern, and clean. For the price, it’s incredibly convenient and offers great value, especially if you’re visiting the parks and just need a comfortable place to rest. The staff were also consistently friendly and helpful, which made the stay even better.

There were just a couple of minor downsides. The hallway near the elevator on the 4th floor had a very strange and unpleasant smell. It was strong enough to notice each time passing through. I’m pretty sure management is aware of it because the hallway doors were kept closed the following day, likely to contain the odor. Hopefully that’s something they’re already working on resolving.

My biggest disappointment actually wasn’t related to the hotel itself. On the first night, our next-door neighbors were yelling and causing a lot of noise throughout the night until around 5 a.m. When I finally contacted the front desk, they responded immediately and handled the situation quickly and professionally. I honestly wish I had called sooner so I could have gotten more rest, but it was my first time experiencing something like that in a hotel.

That said, I don’t blame the hotel at all for that situation. The staff handled it exactly as they should have. If anything, it might suggest the walls aren’t the thickest, but again, the team responded right away when notified.

Overall, I would absolutely consider staying here again for future Universal trips. I’m not really a resort-style traveler, and this hotel checks all the boxes for a park-focused visit: clean, convenient, reasonably priced, and supported by a great staff.

text.text: Room 107 is filled with black mold in shower. Air quality is terrible. Dampness and the smell of bleach hits you as soon as you open the door. Black mold is present between bathroom shower tiles. Management does not care to address the issue and simply says no other guest has complained. Room 107 is a dissiabilty accessible room and maybe isnt rented out often? Will be following up with Hilton to let them know of this issue as this kind of standard and well as a dodging manager ( Manni) trying to not address the issue. We stayed 5 nights inhaling black mold spores and his offer of remediation was to offer one night's comp .  As a courtesy no less. Very condescending manager. I wouldn't stay here again. But the complimentary continental breakfast and its lackluster offerings were nothing compared to the having been exposed to inhaling black mold for 5 days with no possibility of changing rooms as the were sold out.  Will Never again stay  at a Spark Hilton. Hilton is really watering down their brand with thia kind of representation.

If you’re doing Universal it’s seriously a 5 minute drive to the Universal parking lot or a 10 minute drive to Epic.

We already booked a room here for our next trip and can’t wait. Great Value, Great Staff, Great Location!

Wyndham Wingate near Universal
Easily found. Several casual dining places within walking distance. Convenience store and supermarket nearby. The room is setup with a microwave,  a coffee maker and a decent size refrigerator. I might stay again but there are so many good options at same price point in same area. Windham status is not recognized like at a Marriott or IHG property, even Hilton does a better job at recognizing status.

We call this resort our home away from home.   We have been coming here for over 20 years and the rooms are always updated, the service is impeccable and this year they have really paid special attention to entertainment.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Absolutely do NOT get a "Studio Deluxe." It is tiny, dingy, dark, and features a very heavy Murphy bed you have to pull down. And in order to pull it down, you have to disassemble the couch below it. Extremely inconvenient, plus the Murphy bed in our room was saggy and I was rolling into my spouse all night, leading to poor sleep and back pain. Furthermore, after paying for a second room to "upgrade" for a portion of our trip, neither room felt cleaned. The more expensive (but much better layout and experience) "1 Bedroom Deluxe" still had several hairs all over the shower from the previous occupants. The "Studio Deluxe" was so appalling, the housekeeper who came to help us sweep on the second day in the room stated it was in a "terrible state" and "had never seen anything like that before". There were few amenities on-site accept for a pool, jacuzzi, and gym, despite being a "vacation resort."

Side note: the jacuzzi was fun and informative as it was a 2 hour session of Worldmark Timeshare Owners and individuals staying through RCI complaining and warning everyone AGAINST signing up for the Timeshare/becoming an Owner, with a few people even having enlisted attorneys to get themselves out of their bait-and-switch memberships. Of which the whole reason we stayed was because we were lied to and bait-and-switched into a temporary version of their Timeshare called the "Discovery Program", which during our sales presentation (yes you had to go to one of those, AGAIN) the salespeople AGREED it was all a lie and bait-and-switch, and claimed Worldmark is redoing their training programs because it was a rampant problem.
We also had on and off AC issues the whole trip with it vacillating between hot and HUMID and ice cold, with the thermostat locked up behind a locked door and maintenance had to come adjust it themselves anytime we needed a change.

The saving grace was the kindness and attentiveness of the staff. However, this was still the worst hotel experience in recent memory.

We are Blue Green Vacation Club members and would rather pay full price for another resort in Orlando than stay here again.

The suite was not what we requested when we made the reservation a year ago. The response- " we'll what do you want me to do? We're full. "  It was listed as fully handicap accessible but my wheelchair bound mother had difficulty getting in the suite due to furniture that couldn't be moved.  She couldn't get to the master suite bathroom - the bed was too close to the door, and she couldn't rotate her chair. There was no shower curtain in the other bathroom. The shower curtain in the master suite was moldy. There was no fitted sheet for the sofa bed. The replies to the 3 calls (over a 5 hour span) to the front desk were: "we'll send it over when we can", "wasn't it already delivered?", and then "we don't have anyone to bring it over. We have stayed at other Blue Green resorts in Daytona, St. Augustine, and New Orleans. Those have all been high quality. This one in Orlando- "0 out of 10. Would not recommend."

We absolutely loved our stay here all around with so many positive aspects.  For context, we've also stayed at Marriott Harbour Lake and Marriott Grande Vista. Our whole family agreed we loved Cypress Harbour the most and would return here.

A highlight of our stay was DJ Sarah Masters at the pool. Not only did she play great music, but she had such fun games for the kids and kept them entertained and really had great presence!

The main pool by the lobby was lovely. There was a section in it with jacuzzi jets which was really neat as well as a volleyball net and a couple of hot tubs.

We stayed in building 66 and loved the pool near us as well. It had a sauna and a waterfall into the pool which was fun for the kids.

The service here was phenomenal. It was so convenient to text or use the MVC app to request pool towels exchanges and they were rather quick. We love MVCs because of the spacious suites with full kitchens and laundry. So convenient. We even were able to request a blender to make smoothies. Sleeping arrangements and space was great. Although I do like how harbour lake and Grande Vista had two double beds in the second bedroom. This one had a double + sofa bed which was a bit more cramped. The sofa bed was decent though and you could ask for a mattress topper (but we didn't). The huge jacuzzi in the large bedroom was really nice!

The activities club staff were all really great and the kids loved receiving tokens for participation which they then exchanged for prizes which was memorable. We enjoyed learning shuffleboard and the activities staff even took the time to help the kids learn and they were so patient. The activities schedule is quite fun. We loved family puzzle races and just going into the activity centre to see the baby gators or do a puzzle, colour, morning crafts (free of charge (etc). There were playgrounds and mini golf, pool tables, arcade (for a cost) available as well. So much to do that I probably didn't even list.

There is security entrance which made it feel safer.

Loved the boat taxi as well to get from activities to lobby pool area.

The gym was well equipped and the water filter fountain in the gym was fabulous.

Check-in was smooth and easy and the front desk staff were really friendly and efficient.

For the most part we bought groceries and cooked for the week. We did order some kids meals the last day which were pretty standard (burgers, chicken tenders).

Great and convenient location to sea world, groceries and more.

We hope to see you all again! Thank you for a wonderful stay!

However, bring your own amenities or be prepared to drive for some. They have an on-site shop but the prices are outrageous. Lived in Florida for 6 years and never saw anything like it. An ice cream, some hygienic wipes and two toothbrushes with toothpaste came out to be >$50.

We also had to wait almost 40 min in the heat for the cart to come by to pick us up when checking out to go back to the front desks. Had to call twice since the guy was so busy and maybe forgot us.

Our family usually prefers staying at Holiday Inn express hotels because we feel they have been at a pretty consistent comfort and cleanliness standard, with a decent breakfast, everywhere we have traveled. However, after this stay, I've found that my confidence in that consistency is wavering. This hotel is in DESPERATE need of a remodel. Or at the very least, a deep clean. Drives me nuts to pay to park on top of paying for a room. Took two tries to get the toilet that was leaking in the double queen fixed. The breakfast met expectations. We stayed 6 nights and, between the two rooms, paid about $3,000, not including parking. Most staff were attentive, while a few needed to get off their phones. It was conveniently located for Universal Studios, however, the freeway was very loud from our room and I needed ear plugs to sleep. After my stay I wish I had taken the risk with an VRBO or Airbnb. This Holiday Inn express definitely didn't meet expectations.

Our room overlooked EPCOT, and being able to see the area from our room made the stay feel extra special. The rooms were absolutely spotless and felt fresh, polished, and thoughtfully maintained.

One of the biggest highlights of the stay was the lagoon area. It was beautiful, peaceful, and incredibly relaxing — truly one of our favorite parts of the entire experience. It gave the resort such a calm luxury feel while still being fun and welcoming.

What stood out most, though, was the level of service. Every interaction we had with staff felt warm, professional, and attentive without being overbearing. The resort managed to feel upscale while still being comfortable and inviting.

We were especially impressed with how peaceful and refined the overall experience felt compared to many busy Orlando resorts. It truly felt like a luxury escape while still being close to Disney.

This was one of the most memorable hotel stays we’ve had in a long time, and we would absolutely return.

We have stayed at Conrad hotels before and they have never let us down.

I really enjoyed my stay at the Hampton Inn & Suites Orlando International Drive North. It’s a great value if you want to be close to everything without paying resort prices. You’re only a couple of miles from Universal and within walking distance of ICON Park, which made getting around super easy.

The rooms were clean, spacious, and had a microwave and mini-fridge, which I appreciated. Free parking and a hot breakfast (especially the waffle station) were nice bonuses, and not having a resort fee was a big plus.

The only downside was a bit of highway noise and a busy breakfast area in the morning, but overall, it’s a comfortable, convenient stay that I’d definitely recommend.
